claims: The "Arctic Frost" investigation is a Senate Judiciary Committee-led probe.
The "Arctic Frost" investigation is into a 2022 FBI inquiry.
The 2022 FBI inquiry regards the 2020 election "false electors scheme".
The "Arctic Frost" investigation is led by Senator Chuck Grassley.
The oversight alleges that the FBI and Special Counsel Jack Smith improperly targeted hundreds of Republicans.
The oversight alleges that the FBI and Special Counsel Jack Smith targeted members of Congress.
The oversight alleges that the FBI and Special Counsel Jack Smith targeted Republicans via surveillance and phone record subpoenas.
The 2022 FBI investigation opened in April 2022.
The 2022 FBI investigation was later incorporated into Special Counsel Jack Smith's case against Donald Trump.
Oversight revealed the FBI and DOJ obtained records for at least nine Republican members of Congress.
The nine Republican members of Congress consist of eight senators and one House member.
Over 400 Republican-affiliated organizations and individuals were reportedly targeted, according to Senator Chuck Grassley.
Critics, including Senator Grassley, claim the operation was politically motivated.
Critics, including Senator Grassley, claim the operation constituted "lawfare".
Critics, including Senator Grassley, claim the operation was a violation of the Fourth Amendment.
The inquiry highlights roles played by Special Counsel Jack Smith in approving the investigation.
The inquiry highlights roles played by FBI Assistant Special Agent in Charge Timothy Thibault in approving the investigation.
The inquiry highlights roles played by high-ranking DOJ officials in approving the investigation.
Senator Grassley and Senator Ron Johnson are conducting an investigation into the FBI’s actions.
Senator Grassley and Senator Ron Johnson aim to release records.
Senator Grassley and Senator Ron Johnson aim to hold hearings in 2026.
"Arctic-FROST" is a separate, unrelated research project.
"Arctic-FROST" research project is focused on Arctic sustainability.
"Arctic-FROST" research project is based at the University of Northern Iowa.
